scope: Invented logical countercases; no historical probabilities or additional empirical sample

cases.overclaim: Successive local practice implies descent of a later textual institution
cases.construction: A locally maintained drainage operation and an independently composed hymn both exist. No matching technical feature links the hymn to that operation.

cases.overclaim: Population admixture implies transmission of a specified practice
cases.construction: People mix, while the particular lost tool-making recipe is not taught or reacquired. Population mixing and recipe loss are consistent assignments.

cases.overclaim: A borrowed term identifies a named Harappan donor practice
cases.construction: A later speaker borrows a crop name from a neighboring community whose recipe history is unobserved. Contact vocabulary exists without the named donor attribution.

cases.overclaim: An inherited ritual comparison excludes every local contribution
cases.construction: A specialist inherits an office and its verbal formulae, then learns a local water-lifting technique. The role and operation have different route histories.

cases.overclaim: Later synthesis implies that all components were invented late
cases.construction: A compiler arranges an older song and an older procedure under a new explanation. The organization is new while both components predate it.

cases.overclaim: Several agreeing versions increase the independent observation count
cases.construction: A printed edition, its electronic transcription and a translation all preserve the same underlying observation. The lineage set contains one member.
